methodology.scopeRule: Each government in the reconciled six-roster scope has exactly one dated outcome. A legal, statistical, treaty, reservation, or municipal boundary is never evidence of service coverage.

outcomeDefinitions.dedicated-record: Signals has a manually reviewed dedicated public record.
outcomeDefinitions.confirmed-shared-system: An official source explicitly names the government in a shared system or an official router returns an exact government-name result.
outcomeDefinitions.official-referral: The government official site explicitly links or indexes an emergency, alert, evacuation, preparedness, or public-safety source; this does not establish operating area or enrollment eligibility.
outcomeDefinitions.no-public-source-confirmed: The official site and its public sitemap yielded no explicit source under the documented scan; this does not mean no service exists.
outcomeDefinitions.official-site-unavailable: The official roster supplied no website, or the site could not be retrieved; bot blocking and authentication are not treated as proof of absence.

methodology.siteScan: Official homepages and public sitemaps were searched for emergency, alert, notification, evacuation, preparedness, public-safety, and named alert-platform terms. Manually reviewed existing Signals findings override automated outcomes.
methodology.publicationRule: Only manually verified actionable records are published in Signals. Automated audit referrals remain research evidence and never create a public listing or perimeter automatically.

rosterScopes.reconciliationNote: The Province reports 204 First Nations. CivicInfo displayed 208 First Nations-directory records on the review date. The 204-government review scope excludes four explicitly intergovernmental directory organizations—Naut’sa mawt Tribal Council, Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council, Tsilhqot’in National Government, and Tahltan Nation—from the First Nation count; the discrepancy and exclusions are retained here rather than silently discarded.
